# [Implementation] — #328: `sync` must fail closed when an issue cannot be read

## 1. Context

- Smoke section extracted from the archived #328 plan at #364; the body is omitted.

### Manual Smoke Test Protocol

#### Check 1: an unreadable issue is neither closed nor commented and the run exits non-zero

```bash
set -e
root="$(pwd)"
work="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agyloop-sync-failclosed.XXXXXX")"
mkdir -p "$work/repo" "$work/bin" "$work/home"
git init -q "$work/repo"
git -C "$work/repo" checkout -q -b phase/test
git -C "$work/repo" config user.email smoke@test
git -C "$work/repo" config user.name smoke
printf 'probe\n' > "$work/repo/README.md"
git -C "$work/repo" add -A
git -C "$work/repo" commit -qm 'chore: probe'
git init -q --bare "$work/origin.git"
git -C "$work/repo" remote add origin "$work/origin.git"
git -C "$work/repo" push -qu origin phase/test >/dev/null 2>&1
cat > "$work/bin/gh" <<'GH'
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$GH_CALL_LOG"
case "$*" in
  "pr list"*) printf '%s' '[{"number":901,"title":"x","body":"Closes #306"}]' ;;
  "pr view"*) printf '%s\n' 'src/feature.ts' ;;
  *"issue view"*) echo 'HTTP 502: Bad Gateway' >&2; exit 1 ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
GH
chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"
status=0
( cd "$work/repo" && PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" HOME="$work/home" GH_CALL_LOG="$work/gh.log" AGY_SUBAGENT='' node "$root/bin/codeloop.js" sync ) > "$work/out.txt" 2> "$work/err.txt" || status=$?
if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then echo 'FAIL: sync exited 0 after an unreadable issue'; exit 1; fi
if grep -q 'Successfully synced' "$work/out.txt"; then echo 'FAIL: the run still claims success'; exit 1; fi
if grep -q '^issue close' "$work/gh.log"; then echo 'FAIL: an unreadable issue was closed'; exit 1; fi
if grep -q '^issue comment' "$work/gh.log"; then echo 'FAIL: an unreadable issue was commented on'; exit 1; fi
if ! grep -q 'Skipped #306: unreadable' "$work/out.txt"; then echo 'FAIL: the unreadable issue is not in the log'; exit 1; fi
if ! grep -q '#306' "$work/err.txt"; then echo 'FAIL: no warning names #306'; exit 1; fi
rm -rf "$work"
echo 'ok: unreadable issue fails closed'
```

#### Check 2: a readable open issue is closed and commented exactly once

```bash
set -e
root="$(pwd)"
work="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agyloop-sync-ok.XXXXXX")"
mkdir -p "$work/repo" "$work/bin" "$work/home"
git init -q "$work/repo"
git -C "$work/repo" checkout -q -b phase/test
git -C "$work/repo" config user.email smoke@test
git -C "$work/repo" config user.name smoke
printf 'probe\n' > "$work/repo/README.md"
git -C "$work/repo" add -A
git -C "$work/repo" commit -qm 'chore: probe'
git init -q --bare "$work/origin.git"
git -C "$work/repo" remote add origin "$work/origin.git"
git -C "$work/repo" push -qu origin phase/test >/dev/null 2>&1
cat > "$work/bin/gh" <<'GH'
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$GH_CALL_LOG"
case "$*" in
  "pr list"*) printf '%s' '[{"number":901,"title":"x","body":"Closes #306"}]' ;;
  "pr view"*) printf '%s\n' 'src/feature.ts' ;;
  *"issue view"*) printf '%s' '{"number":306,"title":"t","body":"","state":"OPEN","labels":[],"comments":[]}' ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
GH
chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"
status=0
( cd "$work/repo" && PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" HOME="$work/home" GH_CALL_LOG="$work/gh.log" AGY_SUBAGENT='' node "$root/bin/codeloop.js" sync ) > "$work/out.txt" 2> "$work/err.txt" || status=$?
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then echo 'FAIL: a readable open issue must sync successfully'; cat "$work/err.txt"; exit 1; fi
if ! grep -q 'Successfully synced' "$work/out.txt"; then echo 'FAIL: the success line is missing'; exit 1; fi
closes="$(grep -c '^issue close 306' "$work/gh.log" || true)"
if [ "$closes" != '1' ]; then echo "FAIL: expected one issue close, got '$closes'"; exit 1; fi
comments="$(grep -c '^issue comment 306' "$work/gh.log" || true)"
if [ "$comments" != '1' ]; then echo "FAIL: expected one issue comment, got '$comments'"; exit 1; fi
if ! grep -q 'Closes #306' "$work/gh.log"; then echo 'FAIL: the comment does not cite the closing keyword'; exit 1; fi
rm -rf "$work"
echo 'ok: readable open issue closed and commented once'
```

#### Check 3: `sync --dry-run` lists the write without performing it

```bash
set -e
root="$(pwd)"
work="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agyloop-sync-dryrun.XXXXXX")"
mkdir -p "$work/repo" "$work/bin" "$work/home"
git init -q "$work/repo"
git -C "$work/repo" checkout -q -b phase/test
git -C "$work/repo" config user.email smoke@test
git -C "$work/repo" config user.name smoke
printf 'probe\n' > "$work/repo/README.md"
git -C "$work/repo" add -A
git -C "$work/repo" commit -qm 'chore: probe'
git init -q --bare "$work/origin.git"
git -C "$work/repo" remote add origin "$work/origin.git"
git -C "$work/repo" push -qu origin phase/test >/dev/null 2>&1
cat > "$work/bin/gh" <<'GH'
#!/bin/sh
printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$GH_CALL_LOG"
case "$*" in
  "pr list"*) printf '%s' '[{"number":901,"title":"x","body":"Closes #306"}]' ;;
  "pr view"*) printf '%s\n' 'src/feature.ts' ;;
  *"issue view"*) printf '%s' '{"number":306,"title":"t","body":"","state":"OPEN","labels":[],"comments":[]}' ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac
GH
chmod +x "$work/bin/gh"
status=0
( cd "$work/repo" && PATH="$work/bin:$PATH" HOME="$work/home" GH_CALL_LOG="$work/gh.log" AGY_SUBAGENT='' node "$root/bin/codeloop.js" sync --dry-run ) > "$work/out.txt" 2> "$work/err.txt" || status=$?
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then echo 'FAIL: dry run over a readable candidate must exit 0'; cat "$work/err.txt"; exit 1; fi
if ! grep -q 'Would close issue #306' "$work/out.txt"; then echo 'FAIL: dry run did not list the issue it would close'; exit 1; fi
if ! grep -q '^pr list' "$work/gh.log"; then echo 'FAIL: dry run did not read the merged PRs'; exit 1; fi
if grep -q '^issue close' "$work/gh.log"; then echo 'FAIL: dry run closed an issue'; exit 1; fi
if grep -q '^issue comment' "$work/gh.log"; then echo 'FAIL: dry run commented on an issue'; exit 1; fi
rm -rf "$work"
echo 'ok: dry run forecasts the write without performing it'
```

> All three checks create their sandbox under `$TMPDIR` and never touch this
> repository's `.git`, `.agyloop`, or GitHub. Check 2 is the **negative
> control** for checks 1 and 3: it proves the fix did not simply disable the
> close/comment path.
